name: OSCAL crosswalk posture
description: What OSCAL material the estate actually holds, measured, with the path to each file.

upstream.standard: NIST OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language)
upstream.relationship: none. A crosswalk to a public schema is not a relationship with the body that publishes it, and no NIST participation, membership or endorsement is implied.

retracted_claim.why: The cited file layer0_protocol.oscal.json is not an OSCAL document. Top-level keys are constitution, vsm, layers, charters, archetypes, council, temples, guarantees, resonance, sigil. There is no component-definition key and no components array, so the scorecard's own verification one-liner raises KeyError on the file it names. The sigil value is a bare 32-hex string, not a signature.

existing_crosswalk.note: A real crosswalk the estate already holds. Recorded so the gap is scoped correctly: what is missing is an OSCAL component-definition over the GSPC axes, not a crosswalk capability.

what_this_does_not_establish: No NIST endorsement, membership or participation is claimed.
The 97-component figure is not restated here as true. It is recorded as a retracted claim with the measurement that replaced it.
doctrine: A number with no runnable check behind it is not a measurement. Every count on this door names the file it came from.
